sources.name: GitHub issues of floating-ui/floating-ui
sources.version: GitHub REST API 2022-11-28, state as of 2026-11-11
sources.license: GitHub Terms of Service (user content; only facts and our own summaries are kept)

provenance.notes: URL, number, title, state, dates, counts and labels are copied from the API response of each issue. Category, components, summary, resolution and lesson are written by the researcher (tools/extract/field-reports/curation) after reading the issue body returned by the search API and, for the issues listed in docs/research/field-reports.md, the full thread. daysOpen of an open issue is measured to the retrieval date. fixedBy is filled mechanically from merged pull requests that name the issue after a closing keyword. Reports marked needs-review state a cause that the researcher inferred from the symptom without a confirming statement in the issue.

reports.title: Scrollbar not taken into account for RTL direction (scrollbar on the left)
reports.summary: With direction: rtl and overflow: scroll on the body the scrollbar is on the left, and a tooltip placed bottom-end was shifted to the right by the scrollbar's width, because the scrollbar offset was not included for RTL.
reports.lesson: Viewport and clipping-rectangle computation accounts for a scrollbar at the inline-start physical edge in RTL; fixture: overlay alignment with a classic (non-overlay) scrollbar in RTL.

reports.title: Consider RTL directions with the `placement` option
reports.summary: Placement names were purely physical, so a "-start" alignment did not follow the writing direction; the library changed alignment to be logical — a breaking change — after a long discussion.
reports.lesson: Placement is two logical terms (side and alignment); inline sides are resolved by direction before the collision logic runs on physical rectangles. The resolution rule is specified and tested once.

reports.title: arrow middleware does not return correct x and y on rtl
reports.summary: With the document direction set to rtl the arrow middleware returned x/y coordinates that put the arrow in the wrong place.
reports.lesson: Arrow coordinates are physical offsets inside the popup and must be applied with physical properties (left/top), never with inset-inline-start; this is one of the listed exemptions from the logical-properties rule.

reports.title: RTL `useListNavigation` doesn't work with "both" orientation grid
reports.summary: In a grid with both orientations, RTL list navigation moved focus to the right when ArrowLeft was pressed; RTL handling did not cover grid navigation.

fixedBy.title: fix(useListNavigation): incorrect behaviour with RTL grid

reports.lesson: The direction mapping of arrow keys is applied in the shared key resolver, before orientation-specific logic, so grids and lists cannot differ.

reports.title: [DOM] Positioning is incorrect in RTL when document scrollbar is on left side with `fixed` strategy
reports.summary: With the fixed strategy in RTL, when the document itself overflows and its scrollbar is on the left, the floating element was misaligned by the scrollbar's width.

fixedBy.title: fix: correct position when document scrollbar is on left side with fixed strategy

reports.lesson: Same class as the 2020 report: scrollbar-side handling needs a fixture for each positioning strategy (absolute and fixed).

reports.title: Position is not correct when using native popover and RTL
reports.summary: With the native popover API (top layer) the computed position was wrong after switching to RTL; closed as not planned with a workaround.
reports.lesson: Top-layer elements are positioned against the viewport with physical coordinates, and the popup resets any inherited logical insets; fixture: native popover, RTL.

reports.title: Position (via `transform`) is not correct when using native popover and RTL
reports.summary: The same top-layer defect reported again: with a native popover in RTL, a position applied through transform was wrong after a direction change.
reports.lesson: Positions applied with transform assume a known origin; set the base inset explicitly with physical left: 0; top: 0 so that the origin is the same in both directions.
